title: No cooling: contactor coil is open
public_title: Outdoor unit dead, indoor fan runs

equipment.description: 3-ton, 208/230 V single-phase split-system air conditioner, R-410A, scroll compressor, TXV

service_request: Air conditioner stopped cooling. The inside fan blows but the outside unit is not doing anything.

hidden_fault.description: The contactor coil has failed open. 24 V reaches the coil but the contactor never pulls in, so the compressor and outdoor fan get no power.
hidden_fault.repair: Replace the contactor, then confirm it pulls in on a call for cooling and both motors start.

homeowner.name: Marcus Oyelaran
homeowner.persona: Works from home, practical, slightly impatient, gives short answers.
homeowner.opening_line: It quit sometime this morning. Air's blowing inside but it's not cold and the thing outside is dead quiet.
reveals_if_asked: The outside unit is completely silent, no fan and no hum.
Nothing was done to the system recently.
No breakers looked tripped when he checked the panel.
It had been making a chattering or buzzing noise outside for a week or two before it stopped.
The thermostat display is on and shows cooling.
homeowner.red_herring: I figure the compressor finally died, the unit's getting old.
homeowner.rules: Speak as a homeowner, not a technician. Never name the fault or a component. Only reveal a fact when the trainee asks something that would surface it.

checks.label: Check thermostat mode, setpoint and room temperature
checks.result: Set to COOL, setpoint 72°F, room reads 79°F. The thermostat is calling for cooling.

checks.label: Check indoor blower and airflow at the vents
checks.result: Indoor blower is running. Airflow is strong but the air is room temperature.

checks.label: Inspect the indoor air filter
checks.result: Filter is lightly dusty and not restricting airflow.

checks.label: Inspect the indoor coil and suction line for frost
checks.result: No frost or ice on the indoor coil or suction line.

checks.label: Check the breaker and the outdoor disconnect
checks.result: Two-pole 30 A breaker is ON. Outdoor disconnect is seated in the ON position.

checks.label: Look and listen at the outdoor unit from a safe distance
checks.result: Outdoor unit is silent. Neither the fan nor the compressor is running.

checks.label: Inspect the outdoor coil for dirt or blocked airflow
checks.result: Outdoor coil is clean and airflow around the unit is clear.

checks.label: Inspect the thermostat cable and low-voltage connections at the outdoor unit
checks.result: Thermostat cable is intact and the connections are tight.

checks.label: Inspect service valves and line fittings for oil residue
checks.result: Service valves and fittings are dry and clean.

checks.label: Measure voltage across the contactor coil (24 V circuit)
checks.result: 26 V across the contactor coil. Normal is 20 to 30 V.

checks.label: Observe whether the contactor is pulled in
checks.result: Contactor is not pulled in, even though 26 V is present at the coil.

checks.label: Measure line voltage L1 to L2 at the contactor line side
checks.result: 232 V L1 to L2. Minimum operating voltage is 197 V.

checks.label: Clamp the compressor common lead while running
checks.result: 0 A. The compressor is not running.

checks.label: Check charge by the subcooling method
checks.result: Cannot be taken: the system will not run steadily for the required 15 minutes.

checks.label: Turn off the disconnect, lock out and tag it, and verify zero voltage
checks.result: Disconnect is OFF, locked and tagged. Meter confirms 0 V at the contactor line side.

checks.label: Discharge the capacitor with a 15,000-ohm, 2-watt resistor
checks.result: Capacitor discharged across its terminals.

checks.label: Inspect the run capacitor for bulging, dents or leaks
checks.result: No bulging, dents or leaking.

checks.label: Measure capacitance of the dual run capacitor (H to C and F to C)
checks.result: H to C reads 44.6 µF and F to C reads 5.0 µF against a 45/5 µF label. Both are within ±10 percent.

checks.label: Inspect contactor contacts and check coil continuity
checks.result: Contacts move freely by inspection. The coil reads open, with no continuity.

checks.label: Check outdoor fan motor windings with an ohmmeter
checks.result: Continuity between all three leads and no reading to ground.

checks.label: Check compressor windings C-R, C-S and R-S with an ohmmeter
checks.result: All three pairs read near 0 ohms (under 10) and there is no reading to ground.

checks.label: Check low- and high-pressure switches for continuity
checks.result: Both switches show continuity (closed).

diagnosis.repair: Replace the contactor, then confirm it pulls in on a call for cooling and both motors start.

escalate_when: Stop if the replacement contactor pulls in but the motors still do not run; continue diagnosis under supervision.

unsafe_actions.action: Doing any power-off check without first locking out and verifying zero voltage
Touching or testing the capacitor before discharging it
Applying power to a capacitor that is bulging, dented or leaking
Pushing in the contactor by hand or jumpering a pressure switch to force the unit to run
Restarting the compressor without waiting 3 minutes
Adding refrigerant without first checking charge by the subcooling method

safety.criteria: Locks out and verifies zero voltage before any power-off check, discharges the capacitor before touching it, takes none of the unsafe actions, and stops to escalate when the scenario calls for it.

sequence.criteria: Interviews the homeowner first, then moves from observation to simple checks to component tests, broadly following expected_sequence without skipping straight to a guess.

evidence.criteria: Cites the key_evidence checks and their readings to support the diagnosis, and rules out at least one plausible alternative.

outcome.criteria: Names the correct fault and a repair that matches diagnosis.repair, explained clearly enough for the homeowner.

assumptions: Dual run capacitor is rated 45/5 µF, 440 V. The manuals do not state the rating.
Normal compressor running current of 11.8 A is illustrative; the manuals give only the 13.6 A rated load.
Outdoor temperature 88°F and indoor 79°F on the day of the call.
instructor_notes: Correct coil voltage with no pull-in is the service manual's test for replacing the contactor. The trainee should not push the contactor in by hand.
